findings.claim: The current list of ports of entry is 19 CFR 101.4 (101.4(b)(1)).
findings.evidence: The held CFR text (S1 held_path, printed pp. 634-642, 4-1-25 ed.) has the list under '§ 101.3 Customs service ports and ports of entry', paragraph (b)(1) 'Customs ports of entry'; § 101.4 in the same text is 'Entry and clearance of vessels'. The doctrine's own S1 URL (CFR-2025-title19-vol1-sec101-3.pdf), S2 URL (section=101.3), the B01 gap and the O1 gap already say 101.3, so the document contradicts itself. The eCFR versioner for section 101.3 (read 2026-11-05) names the section '§ 101.3 Customs service ports and ports of entry'.
findings.fix: Replace every '19 CFR 101.4' with '19 CFR 101.3' (the list is 101.3(b)(1)), including S1 and S2 citations/titles, M1, B01 description and basis, O1 basis, the .md conclusions, (a), (b), (d) and the undecidable reason.

findings.claim: S16 (TR-CANAL-ZONE) establishes the 'project convention: an order acting on one named person is spent on issue once its single act is performed', and the B17 leads cite it.
findings.evidence: TR-CANAL-ZONE.json is a Canal Zone type rule. Its review_state is 'drafted_awaiting_independent_review', and its legal_effect says 'A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order'. The pinned line is an outlier condition for Canal Zone orders, not a general rule. Coordinator ruling P4 makes PD-CS-ONE-PERSON the governing rule, but the doctrine cites no source for it. The B17 leads stand on the member's own stated effective dates (S0) and P4 (S23); S16 adds no support.
findings.fix: Drop S16 from M5 and the B17 leads, or restate what it establishes as 'outlier condition in one type rule (draft)'. Rest the one-person branches on S0 plus P4 (S23), and cite PD-CS-ONE-PERSON if the coordinator allows citing it.

findings.claim: EO 5577's only operative content revokes EO 5011, so it is spent on issue.
findings.evidence: EO 5577 (jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5577.txt) revokes EO 5011 'and, effective immediately, the said places are restored to and included within the port limits of San Francisco'. The second clause redraws a port's limits. The doctrine treats that kind of act as continuing elsewhere: port-limit extension orders get 'yes' in B01 (EO 4205, 5193, 5445, 6754) or 'open' in O1 (EO 4161, 4343, 4496, 5096, 5320, 5578, 7474). P1 covers restorations to the public domain, and it keeps open any restoration that carries a continuing effect. The doctrine gives no reason why the San Francisco inclusion is exhausted on issue.
findings.fix: Route EO 5577 to open with the port-limit orders (O1), or argue in the basis why including the places in San Francisco's limits has no continuing effect (for example, that it restored the limits that stood before EO 5011, which an unheld instrument would have to show).

findings.claim: EO 538 merges into the parent on issue; gap: 'EO 538's held text is the State Department's description of the amendment, not the order.'
findings.evidence: The held EO 538 text (Wikisource mirror) opens: 'The following is a description by the Department of State of the change defined in the order, not the actual order text.' The doctrine sends EO 99 (covering letter) to O8 and keeps EO 496 (also a State Department description, per the O5 gap) open. A `no` TERM lead needs the order's own operative words, and for EO 538 none are held.
findings.fix: Route EO 538 to O8 (text unusable) until the order's text is held, or explain why a departmental description of the change is enough for a TERM lead when it is not enough for EO 496.

findings.location: B18 date_rule and gaps; M3 effective_date_rule; .md M3
findings.claim: Date recorded is the order date; 'the held texts state effective dates up to about two months later, most often thirty days.'
findings.evidence: P1 dates a spent order by 'the order's own date (or its stated effective date)'. Many B18 texts state a later effective date: EO 2274 (Nov. 30, 1915) is effective Jan. 1, 1916; EO 2303 Feb. 1, 1916; EO 2320 Mar. 1, 1916; EO 4292 Sept. 1, 1925; EO 4319 Nov. 1, 1925; and most 1926-1936 orders are effective 30 days after their date. The longest gap among the 38 held texts is about 32 days (EO 2274), not 'about two months'. Recording the order date puts the end before the abolition took effect.
findings.fix: Use the stated effective date where the text states one. If the machine cannot parse it, use an interval from the order date to the order date plus 32 days. Correct 'up to about two months' to 'up to about one month (32 days, EO 2274)'.

wrong_member_decisions.why: The lead is correct, but its date is fixed on 1927-01-27; EO 4572 took effect thirty days later, so the interval should run to 1927-02-26 (R2).

Not only a revocation: it also includes Oakland, Alameda, Berkeley, Emeryville and San Leandro within San Francisco's port limits, a port-limits act that the doctrine treats as continuing elsewhere. P1 'spent on issue' is unsupported; it should be open with O1 or justified (R7).
The only held text is a State Department description, not the order. A TERM lead needs the order's own words; EO 496 and EO 99 stay open on the same kind of text (R8).
The lead is correct, but the interval end is 1922-06-04, one day after the June 3, 1922 limit the basis itself derives (R10).

summary: The doctrine's structure is sound. Its ACT ends (B02-B12) rest on later orders whose held texts name the member by number or by date and subject, or abolish by name the one port the member created. Its TERM ends match the members' own texts: stated periods, stated retirement dates, pure port abolitions, and pure amendments under P1/P2. Its 32 yes leads match the EO numbers cited in the held CFR port list, and its open groups are stated truthfully. Four errors must be fixed. (1) The port list is 19 CFR 101.3(b)(1), not 101.4; 101.4 is 'Entry and clearance of vessels', and the doctrine contradicts itself because its URLs and gaps say 101.3. (2) B03's date rule fixes EO 2878's end on EO 4572's date, but EO 4572 took effect thirty days later, as the doctrine's own basis and .md say. (3) EO 7463 is at 1 FR 1737, not 1 FR 1502. (4) The .md reports 0 contradictions, but the engine reports 2 (EO 610 and EO 7062, both later amended), which are not disclosed. Further changes: EO 5577's P1 treatment ignores its San Francisco port-limits clause, and EO 538 is decided on a departmental description. The O3 basis cites an unsourced 1965 reorganization plan. S16 is cited for a rule it disclaims. P7 (now in the rulings, whose hash has changed) prescribes a different lead kind for B03-B07. B18 dates ends by order date though the texts state later effective dates, and its 'about two months' overstates the gap, which is at most about one month.
